verdicts.title: _VTableHandle is a redundant single-use wrapper around _BuiltDescriptor (which is already the keep-alive)
verdicts.reasoning: Independently verified from the source. Line 153-157: _BuiltDescriptor holds c, bases, strides, tags, widths, schema, and arrays — every object that must outlive the registration. Lines 806-807: `handle = _VTableHandle(built); _register_with_destroy(db, name, _THE_MODULE_P, built.c.ctypes.data, handle)`. Line 140: `_DATA_ANCHOR[client_ptr] = handle` anchors the wrapper. Since client_ptr is `built.c.ctypes.data` (derived from built.c, which is inside built), anchoring `built` directly would keep exactly the same reachability graph. _VTableHandle is defined once (line 730) and constructed once (line 806); its `_keep = objs` stores only (built,). Removing _VTableHandle and writing `_DATA_ANCHOR[client_ptr] = built` is behaviorally identical. The targets.json note ('genuinely load-bearing, NOT a removable cfunc keep-alive') refers to the _DATA_ANCHOR pattern being needed — not to _VTableHandle as a wrapper class being necessary.

verdicts.title: _VTableHandle.__init__ uses variadic *objs but is only ever called with one object
verdicts.reasoning: Line 737: `def __init__(self, *objs): self._keep = objs`. Line 806 is the only call site (grep confirmed) and passes exactly one argument: `_VTableHandle(built)`. The variadic signature is unused flexibility with no second caller anywhere in the codebase. Finding is accurate, though moot if DES-sqlite_vtable-1 is taken (class would be removed).

verdicts.title: Stale numeric literal in _int_float_cmp comment: 'r >= 2**63' annotates the boundary 9.223372036854775808e18
verdicts.reasoning: Line 498: `if r < -9.223372036854775808e18:   # r < INT64_MIN -> i > r`. The comment 'r < INT64_MIN' precisely mirrors the condition (strict <), which means r == INT64_MIN does NOT take this branch — exactly as intended. The comment does not say 'r <= INT64_MIN'. Line 499: `if r >= 9.223372036854775808e18:   # r >= 2**63 > INT64_MAX -> i < r` is also accurate. Line 502: `# truncates toward zero; r is in [INT64_MIN, 2**63)` then correctly documents that INT64_MIN is reachable via the truncation path. The finding claims the comment 'could read as if -2**63 takes the early branch', but 'r < INT64_MIN' (not 'r <= INT64_MIN') unambiguously excludes the boundary. No comment/code drift exists; the finding rests on a hypothetical reader misconstruing a precise inequality, which is not a real defect.
